decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed the phrase noting that job gains had moderated since early last year, reflecting confidence that the labor market has stabilized at a solid pace.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are moving into better balance.
The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.47% APR costs about $89.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.27% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.88% would fall by about $6.01 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 178k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (February 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -9 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.89%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will wait for clearer evidence of falling inflation before lowering interest rates. The educational forecast model gives the next meeting a 90% chance of a hold and a 10% chance of a cut.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
